title: Obfuscation and encoding: why neither is encryption

videos.script: This string looks secret. It is a database password, written into a configuration file. {{title}} One command, with no key, turns it back into the password. {{decode}} It was never encrypted. It was encoded, in Base64, which is a way of writing bytes as text, nothing more. {{base64}} Here is another one, labelled protected by its vendor. Two commands this time, still no key. {{obfuscated}} The difference between these and encryption is a single question. Is there a secret key, and who holds it? {{test}} If the answer is nobody, then whoever can read the file can read the password. This lesson is about recognising that, quickly, in files you are responsible for.
